content.title: About
content.content: Paratha is an Indian flatbread made from whole‑wheat or white flour, water, salt and sometimes clarified butter (ghee) or oil. The dough is rolled into thin circles and cooked on a hot skillet until golden brown. Paratha can be plain or stuffed with vegetables, potatoes, cheese, and other fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Paratha is commonly served with curry, dal or chutney in Indian cuisine.
There are over 100 varieties of paratha, including layered and flaky versions.
Traditionally the dough is rested to relax gluten, resulting in a softer bread.
In some regions yogurt is added to the dough, making it puffier.
Paratha is a popular street‑food item because it cooks quickly and is served hot.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Paratha provides steady energy through slowly digestible carbs, helping maintain blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: The flour used supplies protein important for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B3 and B6 support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Beneficial fats when cooked with ghee
items.content: Ghee adds short‑chain fatty acids that are easily absorbed.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: A rested dough develops mild probiotic qualities that aid gut health.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Paratha, especially when cooked with oil, is calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid traditional paratha.

items.title: Salt level
items.content: Excessive salt in the dough can contribute to high blood pressure.

items.title: Frying adds fat
items.content: Cooking on a skillet with oil increases fat intake, which may be undesirable on low‑fat diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Paratha is eaten hot, either rolled up, folded, or cut into pieces. It is served with curry, chutney, yogurt, and can be used as a sandwich base. Fillings such as vegetables, potatoes or cheese can be added before folding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked paratha in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage keep it in the refrigerator (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat on a dry skillet to restore crispness.
